data.targetWord: Protections every person is entitled to simply by being human, regardless of their race, religion, gender, or any other characteristic

examples.en-GB: The right to education and the right to be free from torture are human rights.

data.targetWord: The intrinsic worth and value of every human being, which must be respected regardless of circumstances

examples.en-GB: All religious traditions affirm human dignity, though they provide different foundations for it.

data.targetWord: Being treated with the same basic respect and given the same fundamental opportunities as everyone else

examples.en-GB: Equality means no one should be denied opportunities because of their religion or ethnicity.

data.targetWord: Giving people what they specifically need to achieve fair outcomes, which may differ from treating everyone identically

examples.en-GB: Equity means giving a student with a disability extra support to have equal access to education.

data.targetWord: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights — adopted by the United Nations in 1948, setting out the basic rights every person in the world should enjoy

examples.en-GB: The UDHR was created after the horrors of the Second World War to protect all people from abuse.

data.targetWord: An unfair, pre-formed opinion about a group of people without knowledge or evidence

examples.en-GB: Assuming someone is dishonest because of their religion is a prejudice.

data.targetWord: Acting on prejudice by treating someone unfairly because of who they are or a characteristic they have

examples.en-GB: Refusing to hire someone because of their religion is discrimination.

data.targetWord: An oversimplified, fixed image or assumption about a group of people that ignores individual differences

examples.en-GB: 'All teenagers are lazy' is a harmful stereotype that does not represent individuals fairly.

data.targetWord: A quality that the law protects from discrimination in Britain, including age, disability, gender, race, religion, and sexual orientation

examples.en-GB: Religion is a protected characteristic — it is illegal to discriminate against someone because of their faith.

data.targetWord: Prejudice, hatred, or discrimination against Muslims or the Islamic faith

examples.en-GB: Islamophobia includes verbal abuse, denial of opportunities, and violent attacks targeting Muslims.

data.targetWord: Prejudice, hatred, or discrimination against Jewish people

examples.en-GB: Antisemitism includes conspiracy theories, harassment, and violence directed at Jewish people.

data.targetWord: A person who has been forced to leave their country due to war, persecution, or disaster and has been given formal protection under international law

examples.en-GB: Refugees have legal rights under the 1951 UN Refugee Convention.

data.targetWord: A person who has left their country and applied for refugee status in another country, whose claim is still being assessed

examples.en-GB: An asylum seeker is not yet legally a refugee — their claim for protection is being processed.

data.targetWord: The acceptance that a variety of religious, cultural, and ethical views can coexist respectfully in society

examples.en-GB: Pluralism does not mean all views are equally true, but it means all people deserve respect.

data.targetWord: The right protected by law to hold, change, and practise one's religious or non-religious beliefs

examples.en-GB: Freedom of religion or belief means no one can be forced to practise a religion they do not hold.

data.targetWord: Latin for 'image of God'; the Christian and Jewish teaching that all humans are made in God's image and therefore have inherent dignity

examples.en-GB: The doctrine of imago Dei provides a theological foundation for human rights in Christianity.

data.targetWord: Fairness across society; addressing structural inequalities so that all people have access to opportunities and basic rights

examples.en-GB: Campaigning for fair wages and access to healthcare is social justice work.

data.targetWord: Ensuring all people can participate fully and are actively welcomed, regardless of their background or characteristics

examples.en-GB: Inclusion means removing barriers so everyone — including people with disabilities — can take part.

data.targetWord: The duties that accompany rights — what individuals owe to others in order to respect their rights

examples.en-GB: The right to free speech carries the responsibility not to use it to incite hatred.

data.targetWord: The Jewish obligation to give charity and uphold justice; rooted in the idea that giving to the poor is an act of righteousness, not merely generosity

examples.en-GB: Tzedakah is one of the Jewish foundations for social justice and care for the vulnerable.

The Christian and Jewish teaching that all humans are made in God's image is called ____.
Giving people what they specifically need for fair outcomes — which may differ from treating everyone identically — is called ____.

The acceptance that different religious and cultural views can coexist respectfully in society is called ____.

data.title: Arrange these stages in the development of human rights in order
items: The Second World War causes mass atrocities and violations of human dignity
The United Nations is founded to promote international peace and cooperation
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) is adopted in 1948
Nations develop their own laws to protect the rights listed in the UDHR

data.title: Put the stages of seeking asylum in the correct order
items: A person faces persecution, war, or disaster in their home country
They flee to another country and apply for asylum
Their claim is assessed — they are an asylum seeker
If the claim is accepted, they receive official refugee status and legal protections

data.title: Arrange the escalating levels of prejudice in order from least to most serious
items: A person holds a negative stereotype about a religious group
The person makes a prejudiced assumption about an individual from that group
The person treats that individual unfairly — discrimination occurs
The discrimination leads to a hate crime motivated by hostility to their religion
